rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods, Experiments I and II <U+2013> own field trial on 'Fuji'/M9 and 'Fuji'/M26 orchards at Wanju, Korea, with irrigation water measured by flow meter. Q2: Results Experiment I, Table 2 <U+2013> water needed to maintain the same matric potential was 14% lower under surface drip and 37% lower under subsurface drip than sprinkler (299.7 vs 258.4 vs 188.1 Mg/10a); Results Experiment II, Table 5 <U+2013> subsurface drip at 30 cm used significantly less water than surface drip (138.4 vs 288.2 Mg/10a). Q8: Conclusions <U+2013> authors state the results are for a single growing season and later years' data are needed to understand efficiency of the systems. Q9: Table 5 <U+2013> irrigation water reported as mean of three replications <U+00B1> SE (288.2<U+00B1>33.8, 167.2<U+00B1>34.8, 138.4<U+00B1>25.3).
rows.notes: Water use measured by a single method (flow meters) at one site, one crop, plot scale. Tensiometers were used to control irrigation to a set matric potential, not to measure a mechanism of water saving (e.g. evaporation), so Q4 no. The 30 cm burial depth is recommended as 'desirable' but not stated as a requirement, so Q7 no. Table 2 (Experiment I, source of the 37%/27% figures) does not print SE values despite the footnote; SE is printed only in Table 5 for the subsurface-vs-surface drip comparison, which is the same claimed effect. Exp I water differences were not statistically significant (all 'a').

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> own field experiment with weed amount determined per 1 m3 in each treatment. Q2: Results Experiment I, Table 3 <U+2013> subsurface drip had significantly lower weed growth (20.7 Mg/10a) than sprinkler (24.5) and surface drip (23.7). Q8: Conclusions <U+2013> results stated to be for a single growing season, with following years' data needed. Q9: Table 3 <U+2013> weed growth given as mean <U+00B1> SE (24.5<U+00B1>0.37, 23.7<U+00B1>0.32, 20.7<U+00B1>0.41).
rows.notes: Weed reduction is the only pest-related effect; no other pests studied. Single method (weed biomass sampling), one site, one crop, plot scale. No intermediate variable (e.g. surface soil wetting) measured; the mechanism is only cited from Kruse et al. (1990). Methods also state weed growth was controlled during the season, which somewhat complicates interpretation of the weed data.

notes: Primary two-year field experiment (planted 2015, data 2016-2018) on young apple trees at one research station in Korea; full text appears complete. Experiment I compared sprinkler, surface drip and subsurface drip (30 cm); Experiment II compared drip tube depths 0, 15 and 30 cm.
